threads.thread_goal: Align on campaign objectives, audiences and key messages before content creation.

messages.text: Hi team, kicking off the Safety & Sustainability Campaign project. We need to lock in our core objectives and audience segments before we start creating content. I've drafted some initial thinking around who we're trying to reach and what the main safety, security and sustainability pillars should be. Please review and share feedback on the direction. We're working against a 21-day timeline, so let's move quickly but thoughtfully. Key reference: A1 (Campaign Strategy and Messaging Framework) and T1 (core messages) and T2 (strategy and audiences).

Thanks for the kickoff. I've looked at the draft and I think the audience segmentation makes sense at a high level. I'm wondering if we should split out the on-site operations staff separately from office-based teams, since they'll need different channel approaches. Also, what's the tone we're aiming for? Serious and compliance-focused, or more engaging and positive?

On the security side, we need to make sure the messaging doesn't accidentally reveal procedures or vulnerabilities. I'll need to review the final key messages before they go out. The safety and security pillars should probably be kept separate in the messaging so people understand what's a safety issue versus a security protocol.

Good point on the separation. That's actually critical for clarity. Let me revise the messaging framework to keep safety, security and sustainability as distinct pillars with their own key messages. I'll incorporate feedback from both of you and get a revised A1 ready for review by EOD tomorrow.

On the audience split: yes, operations vs. office is important. But we should also think about management layers. Frontline staff, supervisors and senior ops leaders will need different messaging depth. I'd suggest we define at least three audience segments with specific objectives for each. This will help us design the channel mix more effectively.

Agreed on the segmentation. From an events perspective, we'll want to know the audience breakdown early so we can plan the right activation formats for each group. Frontline staff might respond better to quick, practical demos, while management might prefer briefing sessions. I can start sketching out event concepts once we have the final audience segments locked.

That makes sense. So we're looking at: frontline operations, supervisory/management, and office-based staff. For each, we'd have different channel priorities. Frontline might be on-site signage and brief toolbox talks, supervisors get email and manager briefings, office staff get intranet and maybe a lunch-and-learn. Does that align with what you're thinking?

Yes, that's the right direction. Let me update A1 and T2 to reflect those three audience segments and the channel preferences for each. I'll also make sure the key messages in T1 are written in a way that works across all three groups but can be adapted for tone and depth. I'll have a revised draft ready for review by tomorrow afternoon.

Before you finalize, I need to flag that the security examples and scenarios we use need to be vetted carefully. I'll work with security management to pull some real-world examples that illustrate the points without exposing sensitive procedures. That's part of T11. Should have that input to you by end of week.

Good. Once we have the revised A1 with the three audience segments and the security examples from T11, I'd like to schedule a quick review session with the full stakeholder group to sign off on the objectives and key messages. That will be D1 and D2. Suggest we do that by end of week so we can move into content creation next week.

Perfect. I'll have the revised A1 and T1 ready by Thursday EOD. That gives everyone Friday to review before we do a sign-off session. Once D1 and D2 are locked, we can move forward with T5 (digital content kit) and T7 (on-site signage) in parallel.

Works for me. I'll start drafting the channel mix and campaign calendar (A3) in parallel so we're ready to move on D3 next week. I'll need the final audience segments and key messages from A1 to make sure the channel recommendations are solid.

And I'll start working on the event concepts and logistics outline for T3 and T8. Once I have the final audience segments and the channel plan from A3, I can confirm dates and formats. Should have a first draft of the event run-of-show (A5) ready by early next week.

Great. So the sequence is: finalize A1 and T1 by Thursday, stakeholder sign-off on D1 and D2 by Friday, then we move into channel planning (D3), event planning (D4), and quality process setup (D5, D6) next week. I'll start drafting the quality checklist (A2 and T4) in parallel so we're ready to review that early next week as well.

Excellent. That's the plan. I'll send out the revised A1 and T1 by Thursday EOD. Everyone, please review over Thursday evening and Friday morning so we can do a quick sign-off call Friday afternoon. Let's aim for 2pm Friday if that works for everyone.
Friday 2pm works. I'll have the security examples and scenarios from T11 ready by then as well, so we can incorporate any final feedback into the key messages before we lock them in.
Friday 2pm confirmed. I'll have the channel mix draft ready to share as well, so we can start thinking about D3 next week.
Confirmed. I'll have preliminary event concepts ready to discuss on Friday as well.

threads.thread_goal: Define the campaign channel mix, calendar and event concepts.

messages.text: Following up on Friday's sign-off, I've drafted the channel mix and campaign calendar (A3) based on our three audience segments. Here's the thinking: frontline operations get on-site signage, toolbox talks and email; supervisors get manager briefings, email and intranet; office staff get intranet, email and optional lunch-and-learn sessions. Frequency varies by channel and audience. I've also sketched out a high-level calendar that maps content to the 21-day timeline. Please review and let me know if the channel priorities make sense for your teams.

Good foundation. From the events side, I'm thinking we should do three main launch events: one at the largest operations site, one at a mid-size facility, and one at the head office. Each would be tailored to the audience mix at that location. The ops sites would be more hands-on and practical, while the head office event could be a more formal briefing with Q&A. I've drafted some concepts in A5 and T3. What do you think about timing? Should we stagger them or do them all in the same week?

I'd lean toward staggering them slightly. If we do the ops sites first (days 3-5), then the head office event (day 7), we can use the ops events to gather feedback and refine the messaging before the head office briefing. That also gives us time to create content assets in between. What's the logistics footprint for each event? Do we need external vendors or can we do it all in-house?

Good thinking on the stagger. For logistics, the ops sites can mostly be in-house with some basic AV equipment and catering. The head office event might need a bit more polish, so I'd suggest we bring in a vendor for that one. I'm working on the full logistics plan (T8) now. Should have a detailed breakdown of equipment, catering and vendor needs by end of week. That will help us confirm budget and confirm bookings.

Before we lock in the event formats, I want to make sure we have a quality review process in place for all event materials and talking points. That ties into T4 and A2. I'm drafting the quality checklist now, and I'll need to know what assets will be created for each event so I can build the review steps into the checklist. Can you give me a list of what needs to be reviewed for each event?

For each event, we'll need: run-of-show document, speaker talking points, slide deck, any printed materials or signage, and a risk assessment. I'll have those ready for review as part of T3 and T8. The talking points will come from T6, which is being handled by the spokesperson team. So we'll need to coordinate the review process across content creation and event planning.

Right. So the sequence is: finalize event concepts and formats (D4), then create the detailed run-of-show and talking points, then route everything through the quality checklist (A2) before we lock in the final event plans. I'll coordinate with the spokesperson team on T6 to make sure the talking points are ready in time for the quality review.

On the digital content side (T5), I'm planning to create short-form messages for email and intranet, plus longer-form content for the manager briefing guide (T12). All of that will need to go through the quality checklist as well. So we're looking at a pretty comprehensive review process across all channels. That's why getting A2 and the review workflow (T9) locked in early is critical.

Exactly. I'm building the checklist to cover all of those asset types. I'll have a draft of A2 and T9 ready for review by Tuesday so we can get stakeholder sign-off on the review process before we start creating assets. Once D5 and D6 are locked, we can move into full content creation mode.

So for D4, I need to confirm: three launch events (ops sites days 3-5, head office day 7), with in-house logistics for ops and vendor support for head office. Does that work for everyone? I can finalize the event run-of-show (A5) and logistics plan (T8) once we have that locked.
That works for me. I'd also suggest we confirm D3 on the channel mix at the same time. The three-segment approach with the channel priorities in A3 seems solid. Any objections?
No objections from me. The channel mix in A3 is ready to go. I'll start creating the detailed content calendar and asset list once D3 is confirmed. That will feed into T5 and T7.

threads.thread_goal: Set up and validate the quality and compliance review process for all assets.

messages.text: I've drafted the quality and compliance review checklist (A2) and the review workflow (T9). The checklist covers legal, safety, security and brand requirements. The workflow defines who reviews what and in what order. I've also created a tracking mechanism (A6) to monitor the status of all assets as they move through the review process. Please review the draft and let me know if there are any gaps or if the review steps make sense for your teams.

I've reviewed the checklist. The security section looks good, but I want to make sure we have a clear sign-off step for any content that mentions security procedures or incident examples. I'll need to review and approve anything related to security before it goes out. That should be built into the workflow.

Good point. I'll add a specific security review step to the workflow. Any asset that touches on security procedures, incident examples or sensitive protocols gets routed to you for sign-off before it goes to final approval. That should be in T9.

On the brand and messaging side, I want to make sure the checklist includes a step for tone and consistency review. We need to make sure all content uses the key messages from A1 and maintains a consistent voice across channels. Should that be a separate review step or part of the general quality review?

I've included a messaging consistency check in the checklist, but I can make it more explicit. I'll add a specific step that requires all content to be reviewed against A1 for alignment with the key messages and tone. That can be part of the general quality review, but I'll flag it as a critical checkpoint.

For event materials, I want to make sure the run-of-show and talking points are reviewed not just for brand and security, but also for logistical feasibility. Some of the content might require specific equipment or setup that we need to plan for. Should that be a separate review step or part of the event-specific review?

Good catch. I'll add a logistics feasibility check for event materials. That can be a separate step in the workflow where you review the run-of-show and talking points for any logistical implications. I'll update T9 to include that.

So the review workflow in T9 should have these steps: 1) Initial content creation, 2) Messaging consistency check against A1, 3) Security review (if applicable), 4) Logistics feasibility check (if applicable), 5) Brand and legal compliance review, 6) Final approval. Does that capture everything?

That's the right sequence. I'll update A2 and T9 to reflect those steps. I'll also create a tracking template in A6 that shows which step each asset is at and who's responsible for each review. That way we can see at a glance what's pending and what's been approved.
One more thing: what's the SLA for each review step? How long do we have to turn around reviews? With a 21-day timeline, we need to make sure reviews don't become a bottleneck.

Good question. I'm proposing: messaging consistency check (24 hours), security review (24 hours), logistics check (24 hours), brand and legal review (24 hours), final approval (12 hours). That gives us a 5-day turnaround for a full review cycle, which should be tight but doable. I'll document that in T9 and we can confirm it as part of D6.

That's tight but I think it's workable if we're disciplined about it. I'll make sure my team is available to turn around messaging reviews within 24 hours. We might need to stagger content creation so we're not trying to review everything at once.
Agreed. I'll make sure event materials are submitted for review in batches so we're not overwhelming the review process. I can prioritize the critical path items first.

Perfect. So to confirm D5 and D6: we're approving the quality checklist in A2 with the six review steps, the SLAs in T9 (24/24/24/24/12 hours), and the tracking mechanism in A6. Everyone good with that?
Yes, I'm ready to lock in D5 and D6. I'll finalize A2, T9 and A6 by end of day and share the final versions. Once those are approved, we can start submitting content for review.
Confirmed. I'll be available for security reviews starting tomorrow. Just route anything that needs security sign-off through the tracker in A6.
Same here for messaging consistency. I'll monitor A6 and turn around reviews within 24 hours.
And I'll be ready for logistics feasibility reviews. Let's get this process locked in and start moving content through it.

threads.thread_goal: Align on spokesperson materials, manager briefing guide and FAQs.

messages.text: I've drafted the spokesperson talking points and Q&A pack (A4) based on the key messages in A1. The talking points cover the three pillars (safety, security, sustainability) with practical examples and clear language for different audience levels. The Q&A section addresses likely employee questions and concerns. I've also started on the manager briefing guide and FAQ (A8) to help managers brief their teams. Please review and let me know if the content is clear and if there are any gaps.

I've reviewed the talking points. The security section is good, but I want to make sure the examples are accurate and don't inadvertently reveal procedures. I'll need to review the final version against the security examples from T11 to make sure everything aligns. Also, the Q&A section should include a clear answer about what to do if someone witnesses a security concern.

Good points. I'll add a Q&A about reporting security concerns and I'll align the security examples with the final list from T11. I'll also make sure the talking points are reviewed by security before we finalize A4.

On the manager briefing guide, I think we should include some guidance on how to tailor the messaging for different operational contexts. Frontline staff might need more practical, hands-on examples, while office staff might need more context on why these practices matter. Can we add some context-specific guidance to A8?

Absolutely. I'll add a section to A8 that gives managers guidance on how to adapt the messaging for their specific teams. I'll include examples of how to frame safety, security and sustainability differently for operations vs. office staff.
For the event side, I'll need the final talking points from A4 so I can brief the event hosts and make sure they're comfortable with the content. Can you have those ready by early next week?
Yes, I'll have the final A4 ready by Monday EOD. That gives you time to brief the event hosts before the first event on day 3.

Both A4 and A8 will need to go through the quality review process once they're finalized. I'll route them through the checklist in A2 to make sure they align with the key messages and meet all compliance requirements. That should be part of T6 and T12.
Understood. I'll submit A4 and A8 for quality review by Monday EOD. That gives you time to review and get them back to me by Wednesday so I can make any final adjustments before we distribute them.
I'll prioritize the security review of A4 so we can get that locked in quickly. I'll have feedback back to you by Tuesday EOD.
And I'll review A8 for messaging consistency and tone. I'll have feedback by Tuesday as well.

Perfect. So the timeline is: I'll have draft A4 and A8 ready by Monday EOD, you'll review by Tuesday EOD, I'll incorporate feedback by Wednesday, and we can finalize for D7 and D8 by Wednesday afternoon. Does that work?
That works for me. I'll make sure the quality review is completed by Wednesday morning so you have time to incorporate feedback.
Once A4 is finalized, I'll schedule a briefing session with the event hosts to walk through the talking points and Q&A. That should be part of T6.

Good. Once D7 and D8 are locked, I'll send out the final A4 and A8 to the full team and we can move forward with distribution. A8 will go to HR for distribution to managers, and A4 will go to the event hosts and any other spokespeople.
Confirmed. I'll have the security review of A4 done by Tuesday EOD. Once D7 is locked, I'll make sure all event hosts and spokespeople understand the security protocols and examples.
And I'll make sure the messaging in A4 and A8 is consistent with the key messages in A1 and the channel-specific content we're creating for T5. Everything should flow together.

threads.thread_goal: Review launch readiness and define post-campaign measurement approach.

messages.text: We're at day 15 of the 21-day timeline. I've done a pre-launch readiness check and I want to share the status. Most assets are through the quality review process and we're on track for launch. However, I need to confirm the go/no-go decision and lock in the post-campaign measurement approach. I've updated the Asset Review Tracker (A6) with current status and I've drafted the evaluation framework (A7 and T10). Please review and let me know if we're ready to proceed.
Thanks for the status update. Let me review the tracker. Looking at A6, I see most items are approved. Are there any blockers or items that are still pending review?

A few items are still in review: the final event run-of-show for the head office event (A5), the digital content kit for the intranet (T5), and the on-site signage designs (T7). Everything else is approved. The event run-of-show should be done by EOD today, and the digital content and signage should be approved by tomorrow. So we're looking at a full go by day 16.

The event run-of-show is with the quality team now. I expect it back by EOD today. Once that's approved, we can finalize the logistics plan and confirm all vendor bookings. We're on track for the first event on day 3.

The digital content kit and signage designs are in final review. I expect both to be approved by tomorrow morning. Once those are locked, we can start uploading content to the intranet and preparing the signage for printing.
All security-related content has been reviewed and approved. The security examples in T11 are integrated into the talking points and the manager briefing guide. We're good on the security side.

Excellent. So assuming the remaining items are approved by tomorrow, we can confirm D9 (go/no-go) by end of day tomorrow. That gives us day 17-21 to execute the launch and gather initial feedback. Now, on the measurement side, I've drafted the evaluation framework in A7 and T10. The approach includes: engagement metrics (email open rates, intranet page views, event attendance), feedback channels (post-event surveys, manager feedback, employee pulse survey), and a timeline for the evaluation report. Please review and let me know if this covers what you need.

The evaluation framework looks solid. I'd add one more metric: awareness lift. We should measure whether employees can recall the key messages after the campaign. That could be part of the pulse survey or a separate quick poll. Also, what's the timeline for the evaluation report? When do we need to have the final report ready?

Good point on awareness lift. I'll add that to the evaluation framework. For the timeline, I'm proposing we gather data for two weeks after the launch (days 17-31), then compile the report by day 35. That gives us time to collect feedback from all channels and analyze the data. Does that work?
That timeline works for me. I'd also suggest we track which channels drove the most engagement so we can optimize the channel mix for future campaigns. That could be part of the evaluation report.
And for the events, I'd like to capture feedback on the event format and content so we can improve for future activations. I'll include a post-event survey at each event.

Perfect. I'll update A7 and T10 to include: engagement metrics (email, intranet, event attendance), awareness lift (key message recall), channel effectiveness, and event feedback. The evaluation report will be due by day 35. Does everyone agree with D10?

Yes, that covers everything we need. I'm ready to confirm D10. So to summarize: we're on track for a go/no-go decision by end of day tomorrow (D9), and we're locking in the evaluation framework with a report due by day 35 (D10). Once those are confirmed, we can move into full launch mode.
Confirmed. I'll make sure all digital content is live by day 17 so we're ready for the launch.
And I'll confirm all event logistics are finalized by day 16 so we're ready to execute the first event on day 17.
Security protocols are locked in. We're ready to go.
Excellent. I'll finalize A7 and T10 by EOD today and send out the updated evaluation framework. Once we confirm D9 and D10 tomorrow, we're officially in launch mode. Great work, team.
